theme: Zion as mother of all peoples
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 87. This short psalm imagines Zion as the mother city of all peoples, including Israel’s historic enemies. Read slowly. It is a puzzling psalm that becomes clear in light of Acts.
settingTheScene: Psalm 87 is a song of the sons of Korah, a hymn of Zion. It is brief and surprising. God registers people from Egypt (Rahab), Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Cush as born in Zion. These are Israel’s old enemies, and now they are citizens of the city of God. This is the Old Testament’s most vivid picture of the nations coming in.
observation: “On the holy mount stands the city he founded” (v. 1).
“The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwelling places of Jacob” (v. 2).
“Glorious things of you are spoken, O city of God” (v. 3).
“Among those who know me I mention Rahab and Babylon” (v. 4).
“And of Zion it shall be said, This one and that one were born in her; for the Most High himself will establish her” (v. 5).
“The LORD records, as he registers the peoples, This one was born there” (v. 6).
“Singers and dancers alike say, All my springs are in you” (v. 7).
interpretation:
The psalm opens with the city God founded on the holy mount. The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the other dwelling places of Jacob. Glorious things are spoken of her. And then the surprising list begins. God says, “Among those who know me I mention Rahab and Babylon.” Rahab is a poetic name for Egypt. These were the oppressors in Israel’s story, the powers that enslaved and exiled. And Philistia, Tyre, and Cush (Ethiopia) are also named. They are mentioned among those who know the LORD.

Verse 4 ends: “This one was born there.” And verse 5 explains: “Of Zion it shall be said, This one and that one were born in her.” Foreigners are said to be born in Zion. The citizens of Zion include people from every nation. The LORD himself keeps the register: “The LORD records, as he registers the peoples, This one was born there.” When the census is read, the nations are on the list.

This is the idea of the new birth applied to peoples. The New Testament says that believers are born from above (John 3:3). Paul says in Galatians 4:26 that the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother. Hebrews 12:22 says we have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. Ephesians 2:19 says Gentiles are no longer strangers and aliens but fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God.

This is what Acts is unfolding. An Ethiopian official from Cush believes through Philip. Cornelius, a Roman, receives the Spirit. Antioch becomes a church of Jews and Greeks. Psalm 87 pictures the endpoint, in which former enemies sing together and say, “All my springs are in you.” All the sources of joy and life are found in Zion, and Christ is the temple and the center. The gospel does not abolish the identity of nations but brings them into one family, where God registers each as born there.
connection: Isaiah 19:19-25 pictures Egypt and Assyria joined with Israel as a blessing. Isaiah 2:2-4 and 56:6-8 describe the nations coming to Zion. Galatians 4:26 speaks of the Jerusalem above as our mother. Hebrews 12:22-24 says we have come to Zion. Ephesians 2:11-22 says Gentiles are fellow citizens. Philippians 3:20 says our citizenship is in heaven. Revelation 21:24-26 pictures the nations bringing their glory into the city.
application:
Imagine a person from a nation or group you struggle with, and picture them registered as born in Zion with you.

Thank God for the family of the church, which includes people unlike you.

Pray that old enmities in your family or church would be healed in Christ.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for registering people from every nation in his city.
Ask him to make you welcoming.
Thank him that you are born there.
